question: What did each House hearing on the Fed set out to change, and who testified?
answer: The library records 11 House Financial Services hearings on the Fed, from March 4, 2025 to June 25, 2026: 9 by the Task Force on Monetary Policy and 2 by the full committee or a subcommittee. The Task Force heard 45 witnesses, and the library reads 12 of them as 'Analytical'; each card gives the witness's affiliation, a quote, and links to the committee memo and transcript.

sections.title: Hearing by hearing
sections.sub: Each witness is listed with affiliation and the library's stance label, followed by a quote from the hearing. Stance labels are an interpretive reading of each prepared statement.

items.title: Task Force hearing 1: Examining Monetary Policy and Economic Opportunity
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Framing. The opening shot — establish the premise that the Fed is touchable, not sacred.
Norbert Michel (Cato) · stance: Reform
“Congress must first recognize that the Federal Reserve is not an indispensable part of the economy.”
Joseph Wang (Monetary Macro) · stance: Analytical
“[Fed rate policy lays] the brunt of economic adjustments onto blue collar workers and aspiring home owners.”
Donald Kohn (Brookings, ex-Fed VC) · stance: Defender
“Political pressures are invariably on one side — for lower interest rates... but giving in... results subsequently in inflation.”
Mike Konczal (Econ Security Project) · stance: Progressive
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.

items.title: Task Force hearing 2: U.S. Treasury Debt in the Monetary System
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Treasury plumbing. Map the Fed's dependence on Treasury — and Treasury's dependence on someone buying $52T of debt by 2035.
Kristin Forbes (MIT) · stance: Analytical
“Turkey's recent undermining of the central bank's independence contributed to inflation jumping to over 50% in 2022 and 2023.”
Nellie Liang (Brookings, ex-Treasury) · stance: Defender
“Market functioning was restored only after the Federal Reserve itself began purchasing huge amounts of Treasury securities.”
Tom Wipf (UBS / SIFMA) · stance: Industry
“Fix the SLR, recalibrate Basel III, make central clearing work.”
Scott O'Malia (ISDA) · stance: Industry
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.

items.title: Task Force hearing 3: Examining Treasury Market Fragilities
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Treasury fragility. Establish the fragility that justifies the cure — one month after the April-2025 tariff shock nearly broke the bond market.
Darrell Duffie (Stanford) · stance: Analytical
“In the not-so-distant future, Treasury securities will be more widely available in a tokenized form... 24 x 7 x 365 globally.”
Jill Cetina (Texas A&M, ex-Dallas Fed) · stance: Reform

“Movements in gold against the US dollar... suggest the US dollar is not far from being in a currency crisis relative to gold. Since 2011, seven US states... passed legislation accepting gold and silver as legal tender.”
Nathaniel Wuerffel (BNY) · stance: Industry
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Ira Jersey (Bloomberg) · stance: Analytical
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Also quoted: Duffie
“[On April 8, 2025] depth plunged from a norm of about $200 million to a mere $30 million... a full-blown crisis was averted when the Administration postponed its tariff plans.”

items.title: Task Force hearing 4: Less Mandates. More Independence.
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Single mandate. The first cut. Strip the employment mandate — and the hearing came with a drafted bill to do it.
Douglas Holtz-Eakin (Am. Action Forum) · stance: Reform
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Alex Pollock (Mises Institute) · stance: Reform
“The Federal Reserve Board is an agency of the Congress... Congress has plenary power over it. The inflation created by the Fed is in fact a tax on the people.”
Curtis Dubay (U.S. Chamber) · stance: Reform
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Skanda Amarnath (Employ America) · stance: Progressive
“The President's attempted removal of Governor Lisa Cook reeks of desperation and attacks any conventional notion of Fed independence.”
Also quoted: Pollock, quoting McChesney Martin
“You should not have the borrower be the boss of the lender — a... situation known technically as 'fiscal dominance'.”
Also quoted: Bill text (Chairman Hill)
“The Price Stability Act of 2025 amends 12 U.S.C. 225a by striking 'maximum employment, stable prices,' and inserting 'stable prices'.”

items.title: Task Force hearing 5: Examining Primary Dealers and Balance Sheet Constraints
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Dealer capacity. The replacement buyer surfaces: stablecoins as a structural buyer of US debt.
Susan McLaughlin (Yale, 30yr NY Fed) · stance: Analytical
“In the long run, the greatest risk to the resilience of the Treasury market... is the level of the national debt itself.”
James Tabacchi (Indep. Dealers Assn.) · stance: Industry

“We have already seen the impact of [the GENIUS Act] in the short-term Treasury bills market... increased demand by issuers of stablecoins... estimates of growth from about $2 trillion to as high as $4 trillion.”
Laura Klimpel (DTCC / FICC) · stance: Industry
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Haoxiang Zhu (MIT, ex-SEC) · stance: Analytical
“Investors and intermediaries in Treasury securities today bear interest rate risk that is approximately 8 times as large as it was 20 years ago.”

items.title: Task Force hearing 6: Striking the Right Balance Sheet
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Balance sheet / ior. The second cut — and the one place it really is a teardown: dismantle the post-2008 floor system and interest-on-reserves.
Bill Nelson (Bank Policy Inst., ex-Fed) · stance: Reform
“[The balance sheet is] an 'attractive nuisance'... dangerous if misused and... irresistibly appealing to passers-by of impulsive and immature judgment, such as children and congressmen.”
Allison Schrager (Manhattan Institute) · stance: Reform
“QE... poses grave risks to Fed independence. QE is a form of yield-curve control.”
Jim Clouse (Andersen Inst., ex-Fed) · stance: Defender
“Any use of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet to finance fiscal policies... would be wholly inconsistent with the Federal Reserve Act.”
Bill English (Yale, ex-Fed) · stance: Defender
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Also quoted: Nelson
“[The Fed's reserve estimate climbed from $35B to $3T] — 86 times higher than its initial estimate... a floor system requires not just a large Fed, but an ever-expanding Fed.”

items.title: Task Force hearing 7: Revisiting the Treasury-Fed Accord
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Treasury-fed accord. The keystone. Undo the 1951 Accord that gave the Fed its independence — re-subordinate it to Treasury.
Thomas Hoenig (Mercatus, ex-KC Fed) · stance: Reform
“Pressure will only build for the Fed to monetize future debt, thereby leading to fiscal dominance.”
Jeffrey Lacker (Mercatus, ex-Richmond Fed) · stance: Reform

“The minimum level of reserve account balances... is likely on the order of at most a few hundred billion dollars, not three trillion... the Fed holds bills only... the Fed sets just one interest rate.”
Jeffrey Huther (Georgetown) · stance: Analytical
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
William English (Yale, ex-Fed) · stance: Defender
“[The push comes from] Bessent (2025), 'The Fed's New Gain-of-Function Monetary Policy'... [and] Trump v. Cook, No. 25A312 [is] before the Supreme Court.”

items.title: Task Force hearing 8: Examining Derivatives' Role in the Treasury Market
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
Derivatives. The watchdog dimmed, the new rails normalized — the last hearing before the structure field hearing.
Terrence Duffy (CME Group) · stance: Industry
“[A London / Bank-of-England clearinghouse] could... haircut or tear up U.S. Treasury contracts.”
Kevin McPartland (Crisil Greenwich) · stance: Analytical
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Jeff Cranston (Optiver) · stance: Industry
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Yesha Yadav (Vanderbilt Law) · stance: Analytical
“The OFR's workforce is being cut from 196 to ~70... [over] a warning letter signed by Ben Bernanke and Janet Yellen.”
Also quoted: Yadav
“The clearing infrastructure... relies on the very asset whose stability it is designed to protect.”

items.title: Task Force hearing 9: Examining the Structure of the Federal Reserve System
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
BOARD vs REGIONAL. The body preserved and venerated — while the demolition permits are read into the Q&A.
Thomas Hoenig (Mercatus, ex-KC Fed) · stance: Reform
“More and more there's a deferment to the chairman... that culture is weakening the system.”
Esther George (ex-KC Fed) · stance: Defender
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Gary Kelly (Dallas Fed dep. chair) · stance: Defender
“Chair Walsh has already made clear there are policies he would like to review.”
Benjamin Keane (Univ. of Oklahoma) · stance: Analytical
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.
Also quoted: Rep. Warren Davidson (R-OH), building the record in the Q&A

“The Fed has been working on a central bank digital currency... San Francisco's literally hiring people to write code... the balance sheet is 'keystroked into existence'... should we even be paying interest on reserves?”

items.title: Full committee: Future of Payments: Promoting Innovation and Fair Markets
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
The Rails
O'Mara (Stripe) · stance: Reform
“the 1913 framework is now a 'chokepoint'; 'just two banks originate nearly half of ACH volume'; '~80% of eligible institutions have not even connected' (FedNow)”
Anderika (Anchorage Digital) · stance: Industry
“'first federally regulated bank to issue stablecoins... five whitelabel stablecoins'”
Portilla (Davis Polk) · stance: Analytical
“no federal payments charter exists, and a charter doesn't get you a Fed master account — that's the Fed's discretion (cites Custodia)”
Flynn (NCRC) · stance: Progressive
“the OCC stablecoin rule's auto-approval is 'a rubber stamp' while the CFPB is gutted toward 200 staff”
Paridon (Bank Policy Institute) · stance: no label
No highlight quote for this witness in the master.

sources.label: House Financial Services Committee event page (EventID 411134) — not yet opened and checked

items.text: Note carried over from The Hearings page (the library's reading, kept verbatim in the master): AIRED. Chairman Hill; RM Waters. The whole fight: who gets to touch the Fed's payment rails. Stripe (O'Mara) — the 1913 framework is now a 'chokepoint,' 'just two banks originate nearly half of ACH volume,' the US is the only G7 country barring non-bank access, FedNow is dead weight ('~80% of eligible institutions have not even connected'); pass the PACE Act. Anchorage Digital (Anderika) — 'first federally regulated bank to issue stablecoins... five whitelabel stablecoins,' defending the OCC. Portilla (Davis Polk) drew the map: no federal payments charter exists, and a charter doesn't get you a Fed master account — that's the Fed's discretion (cites Custodia). His footnotes name the OCC's Dec-2025 conditional approvals incl. RIPPLE NATIONAL TRUST BANK, Paxos, BitGo, Anchorage. Flynn (NCRC) the lone brake: extend EFTA fraud protections to stablecoins/crypto, put CRA duties on crypto trust banks, and the OCC stablecoin rule's auto-approval is 'a rubber stamp' while the CFPB is gutted toward 200 staff. Storyline: the new-banking-rails turf war + the GENIUS-Act stablecoin charters walking the crypto-rails crowd inside the fence. Full note: 01 - Events / 2026-06-24-1000. Transcript: CAPTURED (full auto-captions, ~2h47m) — search it below. (Paridon's written statement was never posted; her testimony is captured from the video.)

items.title: Subcommittee on Capital Markets: From Wall Street to Main Street: The Future of How America Invests
kv: What it was about (the library's reading)
The Rails
Jonsson (Capital Group) · stance: Defender
“'passive funds don't reduce risk — they lock savers into it.'”
Ptak (Morningstar) · stance: Analytical
“passive beat ~80% of active over the decade (90% in large-cap); fees down to 0.32%”
Quaadman (ICI) · stance: Industry
“TOKENIZATION of real-world assets to 'transform how securities are delivered'”
Renta (Americans for Financial Reform) · stance: Progressive
“passive vehicles are becoming a way for the well-connected to 'offload inflated assets onto everyday investors.'”

sources.label: House Financial Services Committee event page (EventID 411135) — not yet opened and checked

items.text: Note carried over from The Hearings page (the library's reading, kept verbatim in the master): AIRED. Subcmte Chair Wagner; RM Sherman. Active-vs-passive seminar that turned into an alarm. Jonsson (Capital Group) defends active: 'passive funds don't reduce risk — they lock savers into it.' Ptak (Morningstar) with the data: passive beat ~80% of active over the decade (90% in large-cap); fees down to 0.32%; protect Form N-PORT disclosure. Quaadman (ICI) wants the 1940 Act modernized, praises Atkins's 'Make IPOs Great Again,' and flags TOKENIZATION of real-world assets to 'transform how securities are delivered.' Then Renta (Americans for Financial Reform) lit the fuse: passive vehicles are becoming a way for the well-connected to 'offload inflated assets onto everyday investors.' Exhibit A — the SpaceX IPO at $1.77T (after a $4.3B quarterly loss), Musk holding 85% of votes, class actions banned, disputes forced to Texas/arbitration; index providers (Nasdaq-100, FTSE Russell, CRSP) bent their rules to fast-track it — Nasdaq cut seasoning to 15 trading days then won the listing. S&P proposed the same and BACKED OFF after RM Waters leaned on them. Renta's asks: regulate index providers, a federal corporate-governance floor, regulate giant asset managers — and 'Do Not Bail Out Insiders.' Full note: 01 - Events / 2026-06-25-1000. Transcript: CAPTURED (full auto-captions, ~2h) — search it below. Floor highlight: RM Waters — 'Elon Musk is coming for your retirement account'; SpaceX joins the Russell indexes 06/26 and the NASDAQ-100 on 07/06.

uncertain: Stance labels are an interpretive reading of each prepared statement. The labels are the library's, not the witnesses' or the committee's.

All 11 hearing rows are marked 'needs primary source' in the master: the committee's own hearing pages are not linked yet. The video links are the committee's YouTube recordings; the memo and transcript links open the vault's saved copies.
'What it was about' is the library's reading of each hearing's purpose, carried from The Hearings page; it is not the committee's wording.

The committee's September 2026 schedule listed a tenth Task Force hearing, 'Examining the Future of Central Banking', for September 23, 2026. The master has no row for it and no hearing after June 25, 2026, so whether it (or any later Task Force hearing) was held is unconfirmed.
No caption transcript is on file for the hearings of January 14, 2026 and April 29, 2026.

catalog_context.title: How Congress is building the new money plumbing
catalog_context.answer: A big rebuild of U.S. financial plumbing is under way, but not as one bill: Congress, a dozen agencies and market utilities like DTC are each moving separate pieces that are converging.

catalog_context.title: A catalog of saved hearing memos, testimony and bills, from late 2024 to mid-2026
catalog_context.answer: Katie's vault keeps a wide shelf of congressional hearing documents beyond the House Oversight set. The study keeps each source type's limits attached: a committee memo, prepared testimony and a bill text are different kinds of evidence, not transcripts of…
